takeaways.title: Genuine leaks/vampires hide in low-baseline meters
takeaways.body: The meters worth acting on are ones that normally sit near zero and suddenly spike: Habitat Warehouse Building (26→653 kWh, 25×), Tire Mart #5 (10×), Pantops #102 (176×). Big summer-AC / winter-heat swings on already-large meters are seasonal and expected.

takeaways.title: Two live water-leak signatures on the City of Staunton side
takeaways.body: 802 Richmond spiked to 41 HCF from a 0–1 baseline in May 2026 — the city printed a 'possible leak' notice on the bill. Genesis (823 Richmond) shows 180 & 121 HCF in mid-2023 vs a 3–4 baseline. Both are worth a physical check.

takeaways.title: Gas peaks are seasonal — read them as heating, not anomalies
takeaways.body: Every gas meter peaks in winter (heating) and falls to near-zero in summer. Those 3–20× winter ratios are normal. The one real gas story is Charlottesville's Flow Center Lot, whose usage collapsed from ~16–20k cu.ft/mo in 2023 to near-zero by 2024.

takeaways.title: Several accounts closed or went vacant mid-window
takeaways.body: 2655 S Main dropped to 0 kWh in spring 2026 (vacant). SVEC center, Pantops, Woodstock, and Shops at Waynesboro accounts closed ~Jan 2026. These flat-line drops are account closures, not meter failures.

quality.title: Different utilities use different units — never sum across them
quality.body: Water is HCF (Staunton) and CCF (Danville) — those are equivalent (hundred cubic feet). Gas arrives in three units: CCF, Therms, and raw Cu.Ft. Electric is kWh throughout. Charts and tables keep each series in its own unit; totals are never mixed across units.

quality.title: Some properties have multiple meters
quality.body: Heritage (elec #A/#B), Tire Mart (House + #5), Pantops (House + suites 102/107/108), and the Habitat warehouse each carry more than one service point. They appear as separate rows/series so a small tenant meter doesn't hide behind a large one.

quality.title: Coverage is uneven by design — utilities come from different vendors
quality.body: A property only shows a utility if that utility is billed through a vendor we pulled. Water = City of Staunton only; most electric = Dominion VA; gas = Columbia/Danville/Charlottesville. So a Staunton property may have water+electric but no gas simply because it has no gas service — the coverage grid below distinguishes 'no service' from 'not yet pulled'.

quality.title: Flow properties were relabeled to match the directory
quality.body: 1289 Stony Point was mislabeled 'Flow Center Lot' and is now correctly 'Flow Corner' (Yardi had renamed the property mid-stream; same physical meter). Flow Center Lot (1311) has no Dominion electric meter — it is gas-only.

recon: Flow properties per property directory: Flow Corner = 1289 Stony Point Rd · Flow Center Lot = 1311 Stony Point Rd · Flow Back Lot = 1321 Stony Point Rd.

Flow Corner (1289): outside-lights meter, Dominion acct 002898924267 — full series above (relabeled from "Flow Center Lot (lights)"). The separate 1289 main-building electric meter closed 2024-07-01 (final bill); not tracked.
Flow Center Lot (1311): NO Dominion electric meter in vendor ledger 10456 — this lot is gas-only (see Charlottesville Gas sheet). No electric series to add; nothing missing.
Flow Back Lot (1321): correctly labeled. Dominion acct 210022720283 — intermittent (closing bill 2024-11, reopened 2026-03).

Wells Property/Bookstore (707A Richmond Ave): CLOSED accounts — Dominion electric final invoice 2024-01-04 (3 bills, late 2023), Columbia gas final 2023-12-21 (3 bills). No active usage; not backfilled (ledger shows $ only and meters closed before the tracking window).
nextsteps: Capture usage at bill-entry going forward (a Custom Data field in Yardi or a shared sheet) so no future backfill is ever needed — the on-bill usage tables make this ~30 seconds per bill.
Physically check 802 Richmond and Genesis for water leaks — both show live leak signatures and 802 Richmond carries a city leak notice.
Confirm the 153 Crown Dr (Danville) electric ramp (600→28,200 kWh over 6 months) is expected new-tenant load, not a metering or billing error.
Standardize gas units: bills arrive in CCF (Danville), Therms (Columbia), and raw Cu.Ft (Charlottesville). Pick one (Therms) and convert on entry so gas is comparable across vendors.
Two utility vendors (Washington Gas, Central VA Electric Coop) have zero invoices in Yardi — verify whether any property is actually served by them and billed elsewhere.
